name: Pastebin

sources.title: Pastebin homepage — guest 'New Paste' form with exposure options (Public/Unlisted/Private) and signup prompts

requirements: Pastebin is a text/code-paste host, not a product directory — there is no 'submit product' flow
Guests can create pastes without an account, but guest pastes cannot be edited or deleted later
Paste exposure choices: Public (listed in the public archive), Unlisted, or Private (members-only folders exist)
PRO membership exists (Markdown syntax highlighting is PRO-only, among other perks)
preparation: Text content for the paste (a product description, changelog, or code snippet containing the product URL)
Decide exposure: Public is the only exposure that surfaces in the public archive
workflow: Open pastebin.com — the New Paste form is on the homepage
Paste content, optionally pick a category, syntax highlighting, expiration, and set Paste Exposure to Public
Create the paste; note the URL — guests lose all edit/delete control
Alternatively sign up (email or Facebook/Twitter/Google OAuth) to retain edit/delete and use folders
watchFor: Guest pastes are permanent and uneditable — never paste anything sensitive
Public archive spam is heavily abused; links in pastes carry little to no SEO value and may be nofollowed
Burn-after-read and expiration options can silently kill the listing — pick 'Never' if persistence matters
Not a real launch destination; only useful as a supporting citation at best
countsAsLive: The paste URL resolves publicly and appears in pastebin.com/archive (Public exposure only)
unknowns: Whether public pastes remain indexed by search engines at all
